findings.claim: The content page's three-step hierarchy is built from size and centring alone, with no colour used to rank.
findings.evidence: Title 'All 32,223 Places on One Map' at roughly 56px heavy geometric sans; subtitle at about 26px normal weight; byline at about 13px letterspaced small caps. All three near-black brown on white, centred on one axis.

findings.claim: On the desktop home page the top level of hierarchy is a photograph, not type; the orderly type ladder beside it loses.
findings.evidence: Headline 'The World's Hidden Wonders' at about 42px on two lines in the left half; a roughly 755x500px 'Place of the Day' photograph fills the right half and carries the only saturated colour on the screen.

findings.claim: Every home-page section uses one repeated device: a small letterspaced kicker above a large two-tone heading whose last word turns tan.
findings.evidence: 'EDITOR'S PICKS' over 'Begin Your Journey'; 'ATLAS OBSCURA COMMUNITY' over 'Featured Members'; 'HIDDEN WONDERS' over 'Explore the Atlas'; 'BOOKS AND BOX SETS' over 'Complete Your Bookshelf'. The final word is tan in each.

findings.claim: On the desktop home page the eye lands on the Place of the Day photograph, not on the headline and not on the search bar; the search bar is a low-contrast outlined pill that reads as subordinate to both.
findings.evidence: The photograph occupies about 53 percent of viewport width (754px of 1440) and carries the only saturated colour on the screen; the search bar is a 456px white pill with a thin grey outline, low in the left column, with no fill. The original 'the search bar is the fourth thing seen' is removed: a still capture can show what dominates, not a reading order past the first landing.

findings.claim: On the mobile home page two filled action pills sit above the headline and the search bar and take the first read.
findings.evidence: 'Places near me' (dark filled) and 'Random place' (outlined) sit directly under the header at about y=147; the search bar lands about 465px down an 812px screen.

findings.claim: On the desktop content page the title is clearly dominant, but the first screen is not bare: a filled promotional button sits in the share row and the saturated map fills the bottom 200px of the viewport.

findings.claim: On mobile nothing persists during a 15,358px scroll; there is no indication of what page you are on.

findings.claim: Inferred: exactly one copy control exists on the content page, presumably inside the SHARE menu; there is no per-block or per-field copy affordance.

findings.claim: Inferred: the recorded fixed layer is almost entirely dormant, and the visible 48px article bar cannot be identified in it.
findings.evidence: domEvidence stickyOrFixedCount is 23; 20 measure height 0 at rest (AdBlockModal, lightbox-modal, subscription-ask-modal, onetrust panels, and the single position:sticky entry). So the original 'the visible strip is the only one that paints' is wrong twice: the strip is not matchable to any recorded entry, and a full-height recorded entry paints nothing.

findings.claim: Inferred: light-only. The dark bands on the home page are section grounds, not a dark theme.
findings.evidence: domEvidence prefersColorScheme.found is false across 54 stylesheets (5 unreadable), htmlAttributes.dataTheme and class are null, and no theme control appears in any capture.

findings.claim: Inferred: search is a real inline input, not a command palette.

findings.claim: Borrow the labelled stat cell for structured data blocks: a 10px letterspaced grey label above a bold numeral, hairline-boxed, rows ruled.
findings.evidence: 'PLACES 47 / STORIES 3' pattern in the destinations rail reads as a table without being one and stays legible at four rows per 675px (169px row pitch, corrected from 570px); a programme with three counted fields would produce a visibly shorter block than one with six.

findings.claim: Borrow the plain columned link table for browse/filter: heading, hairline rule, text links in columns, no thumbnails.
findings.evidence: Top Countries / Top Cities fits 36 navigation targets in about 310px of height and is the only region of either page whose markup would raise a text-to-HTML ratio rather than sink it.

findings.claim: Borrow the classifying kicker so a model organism or evidence tier is read before the claim and cannot be mistaken for it.
findings.evidence: A 10-11px letterspaced category word sits tight above every title at every level of both pages and consistently classifies before the title is read.

findings.claim: Borrow the scroll strip that names the page: a 48px bar carrying only the mark and the current page title.
findings.evidence: Identical at 50 and 90 percent depth; it answers 'what am I reading' eleven screens down. It is not a contents rail and does not substitute for the unassigned rail surface.

findings.claim: Borrow the mobile footer accordion for collapsing repeated navigation markup without deleting it.
findings.evidence: Five closed chevron rows at 375px where desktop shows an open five-column table.

findings.claim: Borrow the reserved image box so a card does not reflow when its picture arrives.
findings.evidence: The Keep Exploring boxes are identical in size and position with and without the photograph.

findings.claim: Avoid putting a photograph beside the search bar: this is the exact failure the frozen home constraint exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: A 754x500px image in the right half carries the only saturated colour on the screen and takes the first read; the search field is a 456px outlined pill with no fill. 'The search field is fourth' is removed - a still capture cannot establish reading order past the first landing.

findings.claim: Avoid action pills above the primary action; Atlas puts two above both its search bar and its article title.
findings.evidence: 'Places near me' and 'Random place' are the only filled shapes on the mobile first screen and push the content title to about 40 percent down.

findings.claim: Avoid signalling provenance by one word in identical type; for a health-evidence site this is disqualifying.
findings.evidence: 'BY ATLAS OBSCURA' and 'SPONSORED BY VISIT SUN VALLEY' share slot, size, colour and letterspacing.

findings.claim: Avoid rendering a filter control with a silent empty result; either omit the control or say what it found.
findings.evidence: 'Explore the Atlas' with a 'View all Places' link and FEATURED / MOST RECENT pills, followed by about 80px of blank ground to the section's end and no message anywhere. (Corrected from ~200px.)

findings.claim: Avoid a form inside the reading column; on a dossier that position belongs to evidence.
findings.evidence: The newsletter panel sits at prose width in prose position, one paragraph into a five-paragraph article, at both widths.

findings.claim: Avoid recommendation grids as the bulk of the page - about 57 percent of the desktop content page's height and about 85 percent of the mobile page's, with the mobile midpoint holding no article text.
findings.evidence: The article's last line sits at about y=2,010 of a 4,673px desktop page (43 percent, not the 20 percent first reported) and about y=2,325 of a 15,358px mobile page (15 percent); content-375-scroll-50, the exact midpoint, shows six video cards and no article text. The eager-image and ratio figures that accompany this (imgCount 513, imgLazyCount 0, textToHtmlRatio 0.0015) are domEvidence, not visual observations, and are now declared as such.

findings.claim: Avoid coloured chrome as the loudest thing in a long scroll; a sticky strip's icons should take the text colour.
findings.evidence: Three brand-coloured filled share tiles (Facebook, Twitter, Reddit) plus a plain dark mail glyph in the persistent bar, on a page whose palette is otherwise brown, tan and white.

findings.claim: Avoid 10px side margins for prose at 375px while cards below keep their gutters.
findings.evidence: Body text runs edge to edge from x=10 while the video cards keep about 12px gutters and internal padding.

findings.claim: Avoid reserved empty advertising space as a layout element.
findings.evidence: At least three labelled ADVERTISEMENT strips of about 110px each on the desktop home page, roughly 330px of held-open blank. The 245px unlabelled band above the header is excluded: manifest bannerActions records a banner left standing on all four passes, so that band cannot be read as design.

findings.claim: The page states its central count three different ways and dates none of them: the h1 says 32,223 places, the opening paragraph says 'more than 32,100', and the map renders its own cluster totals.
findings.evidence: h1 'All 32,223 Places on One Map' (content-1440-tile-01); first paragraph 'There are now more than 32,100 incredible hidden wonders listed in the Atlas' (content-1440-tile-02); the map's visible cluster pins read 2863, 1204, 1097, 497, 158 and so on. No 'as of' date appears anywhere. For an RNAWiki dossier that states counted facts - trials, sources, claims, reviewers - the number must be derived once from the published record and carry the date it was computed, or the page contradicts itself in public and the reader cannot tell which figure is current.

findings.claim: Atlas has a counted and an uncounted browse idiom on the same site and gives the counted one to marketing: fourteen flat category pills follow the article, while the destinations rail gives every entry a labelled count.
findings.evidence: Fourteen identical outlined pills - LIST, INVENTIONS, MEMENTO MORI, MAPS, GHOST TOWNS, CATACOMBS AND CRYPTS, NATURAL WONDERS, COLLECTIONS, MONUMENTS, ABANDONED, NATURE, ARCHITECTURAL ODDITIES, ANIMALS, ARCHITECTURE - all one weight, in no visible order, with no counts, wrapping over four rows below the article (content-1440-tile-03). The home-page rail gives every destination 'PLACES 74 / STORIES 2' in hairline-boxed cells (index-1440-tile-03). RNAWiki's indication and tag chips should carry the count in the rail's cell, so a chip leading to two programmes is visibly not a chip leading to forty, and an empty facet is visible before it is clicked.

findings.claim: The scope path exists only on the first screen: the breadcrumb naming where the article sits is 11px grey caps above the h1, and the 48px scroll strip that replaces it carries the title without the path.
findings.evidence: content-1440-tile-01 shows 'HOME > STORIES > FEATURE > ALL PLACES IN THE ATLAS ON ONE MAP' in about 11px letterspaced grey caps at y=362, directly above the h1; content-1440-scroll-50 and -scroll-90 show the persistent strip carrying only the mark and 'All Places in the Atlas on One Map'. Ten screens down, nothing says which section the page belongs to. On RNAWiki a reviewed conclusion belongs inside one programme scope - indication, population, dose, trial set - so that scope line must travel with the title in the persistent strip, not appear once above it and disappear.

phase2.argument: Phase 2 names atlasobscura.com only in the browse/filter row, marked 'half overturned: Atlas Obscura dropped', on the number 0.17 percent text-to-HTML against a corpus target that must rise from 8.3 percent. Looking at it strengthens that drop and adds three reasons the number could not give. First, the visible form of the ratio is not merely heavy markup: on mobile the article ends at about 15 percent of a 15,358px scroll and content-375-scroll-50, the exact midpoint, contains six video thumbnails and no article text (F10, A6). Verification corrected the desktop half of this - the article there ends at about 43 percent, not 20 - so the imbalance is a mobile finding, not a uniform one. Second, the one browse surface Atlas actually renders is empty: 'Explore the Atlas' shows its FEATURED / MOST RECENT pills over about 80px of blank ground with no message (F29). A site that cannot show its own filter results cannot govern our filter surface. Third, Atlas makes editorial and paid provenance visually identical, same slot and same 10px letterspaced caps (F28) - a governing-reference-level defect for a health-evidence site, not a detail. It earns no surface and should not be assigned to one it does not hold. The drop should not be total, though: two detail patterns survive under other sites' governance - the labelled stat cell for structured data blocks (B1, under stripe.com/docs) and the plain columned link table for browse (B2, under awwwards.com). Both are the same idea, and it is the idea Atlas is worst at overall: say it in text in a table, not in a photograph in a card.

Plain columned link table with a heading over a hairline rule, no thumbnails, 36 targets in ~310px (index-1440-tile-07) - browse/filter, corroborating awwwards.
Classifying kicker tight above every title, so model organism or evidence tier is read before the claim (content-1440-scroll-50, index-1440-tile-03) - dossier reading column and browse.

Reserved image box that does not reflow when the picture arrives (content-1440-tile-03 vs content-1440-scroll-50) - any card grid.

Action pills above the primary action and above the page title (index-375-tile-01, content-375-scroll-00) - home and dossier reading column.
Provenance signalled by one word in identical type (index-1440-tile-03) - reading column, data blocks, citation map.
A filter control rendering a silent empty result (index-1440-tile-04) - browse/filter.
A form inside the reading column one paragraph in (content-1440-tile-02, content-375-tile-03) - dossier reading column.
Recommendation grids as ~57 percent of the desktop page and ~85 percent of the mobile page (content-375-scroll-50, content-375-full) - all surfaces.
Brand-coloured chrome as the loudest thing in a long scroll (content-1440-scroll-90) - contents rail.

A scope path that appears once above the title and does not survive the scroll (content-1440-tile-01, content-1440-scroll-50) - dossier contents rail.

bannersStanding: manifest bannerActions records a banner left standing on all four passes (index-1440, index-375, content-1440, content-375) because no permitted refusal control was found; NO consent banner content is visible in any capture. The hairline-bounded strips labelled ADVERTISEMENT are the site's own reserved slots and are judged as design. VERIFIER CORRECTION: the unlabelled empty band at the top of every capture (~245px desktop, ~50-70px mobile) is NOT judged as design - an unpopulated container of unknown identity is exactly what a standing banner would produce, so it has been removed from F16 and A9.

verification.verifiedBy: independent verifier (all 8 required desktop captures, all 3 required mobile captures, plus index-1440-tile-02/05/07/10, index-375-full/tile-15, content-1440-tile-04/05, content-375-tile-03/19/scroll-90, content-375-full viewed directly)
notes: REFUTED F24 ('every other image decorates or baits... the visible form of the site's 0.0015 text-to-HTML ratio'). Two grounds: the load counts and the ratio are Phase-1/domEvidence numbers presented as a visual observation with inferred:false and no domEvidenceKeys; and 'every other image' is contradicted by the destination-rail thumbnails and the Read Next thumbnail, which identify what they link to. The verifiable half - content-375-full is a near-continuous photographic column - is retained in the corrected A6, which now declares its DOM keys.

Largest numeric correction: the desktop content page's article ends at about y=2,010 of 4,673px (43 percent), not 20 percent, so recommendation and promotion is about 57 percent of desktop height, not 80. The 80/20 shape is real only at 375px (article ends at about y=2,325 of 15,358px, 15 percent). F10, A6 and the phase2 argument were rewritten; the mobile-midpoint evidence is unaffected and stands.

Method correction affecting F16 and A9: the unlabelled ~245px band above the header was counted as reserved advertising space and as design. manifest bannerActions records a banner left standing on all four passes, so an empty container of unknown identity is exactly what would appear there. The band is removed from both findings; the hairline-bounded strips actually labelled ADVERTISEMENT stay, and there are at least three of them on the desktop home page (index-1440-tile-02, -03, -05), not two, so the labelled reserved space is about 330px.

F22 overstated the sponsored/editorial resemblance. The heading match is real ('From Around the Web' equals 'Keep Exploring' in size, weight and alignment) but the Taboola cards use serif titles, the advertiser in small caps below, and 'Learn More'/'Click Here'/'Read More' buttons, while the Keep Exploring cards use bold sans titles with a category kicker above and no button. They are distinguishable, just not disclosed. The site's genuine provenance failure is F28 on the home-page rail, which is CONFIRMED exactly as written and is the finding RNAWiki should carry.

F33 was treated as a design finding; the same Google Play badge loads correctly in index-375-tile-15, so it is a capture-time failure, exactly the artefact the viewer correctly excluded at F25. Rewritten to report only the fallback's styling.

F37's 'the visible strip is the only one that paints' does not hold: the single position:sticky entry is recorded at height 0, so the painting 48px bar is not matchable to any of the 23 recorded elements, and the one full-viewport-height entry (nolt-modal, 900px) paints nothing in any capture.
